chunks: How long shall I accord you consideration that is accorded to camels with hollow humps, or to worn clothes!
Whenever they are stitched on one side, they give way on the other,
Whenever a vanguard force of Syria hovers over you, everyone of you shuts his door,
And hides himself like the lizard in its hole, or the badger in its den.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الشَّامِ: People of Syria (referring to the Syrian army in the context of early Islamic conflicts)
key_terms.الضَّبَّةُ: The lizard (specifically the gecko or small lizard)
key_terms.الْبِكَارُ الْعَمِدَةُ: Camels with hollow humps (a specific breed/type known for this trait)

ai.seo_question: What metaphor did Imam Ali use to describe the cowardice of his companions in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This passage, delivered during the period of internal strife (Fitna) following the Battle of Siffin, highlights the fragmentation of the Muslim community as individual self-preservation superseded collective jihad. Sharif al-Radi’s compilation preserves this vivid imagery of 'hollow-backed camels' and 'torn garments' to critique the loss of spiritual and martial cohesion among the companions. The metaphor underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on unity (Jamāʿah) and the danger of retreating into private spheres when the community faces external or internal threats.
